title: The Charge Base Retained on a Granite Ridge Season Pass Given Up
content:
The base from which the charge retained on a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass is worked out is taken as follows.

**First.** Where the pass record was opened as a renewal of a pass held in the preceding season and the price committed to stands below the tier's standard season price, the charge base is the tier's cancellation fee reduced in the proportion the price committed to bears to the tier's standard season price.

**Second.** Where the price committed to stands at or above the tier's standard season price and the pass became scannable at least 7 days before the handling date, the charge base is the tier's cancellation fee taken once and a tenth, a multiple of 1.1.

**Otherwise.** In any other case the charge base is not moved by this rule.

### The conditions set out

| How the pass record was opened | The price committed to against the tier's standard season price | Days since the pass became scannable | The charge base |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a renewal of a pass held in the preceding season | below it | any number | the cancellation fee in the proportion the price committed to bears to the standard season price |
| either | at or above it | at least 7 | the cancellation fee at a multiple of 1.1 |
| either | at or above it | fewer than 7 | not moved by this rule |
| not such a renewal | below it | any number | not moved by this rule |

The count of 7 days runs from the day the pass became scannable to the handling date, and the day the pass became scannable is where the count starts.

### Worked on hypothetical figures

A Granite Ridge Summit Pass, whose standard season price is 1149.00 and whose cancellation fee is 125.00.

On a record opened as a renewal and committed to 1034.10, which is nine tenths of that standard season price, the charge base is 125.00 taken in that proportion, which is 112.50.

On a record committed to 1149.00 that became scannable 20 days before the handling date, the charge base is 125.00 at a multiple of 1.1, which is 137.50.
